findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the ice machine to be soiled with rust in the interior baffle of the machine. The metal panel at the top of the ice basin appears to be rusted. Inspector recommends emptying the machine, scrubbing any observed rust, and sanitizing thoroughly. If the rust cannot be removed by cleaning, replacement of the damaged parts will be required. The inspector will follow-up on October 20, 2026 to ensure the interior of the ice machine is clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The inspector observed the condenser unit of the walk-in cooler and freezer to be leaking water. The staff have placed plastic bins below the condenser to capture any leaking water. Inspector recommends continuing this process until the condenser is repaired. Repair of both the walk-in cooler and freezer is required prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed multiple employees put on glove without first washing hands. Wash hands before putting on new gloves. Discussed proper hand washing technique and glove use with employee.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed knife sanitizer at prep line to measure inadequate quaternary ammonia concentration. Ensure sanitizer tablets are fully dissolved so that concentration is adequate and knives are properly sanitized. The sanitizer was replaced during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed a large hole in the wall to the left of the mop sink. The coving around the mop sink was also starting to separate from the wall. Ensure the facility is maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed personal items (jacket, hat, etc.) stored on dry shelving holding chips and other food items. Ensure personal items are stored away from food to prevent cross-contamination. The items were moved during the inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee put on glove without first washing hands. Wash hands before putting on new gloves. Discussed proper hand washing technique and glove use with employee. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizing solution available for use during food preparation and service. Sanitizer solution was made during inspection and tested at 200 ppm quaternary ammonia.
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. 
(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee wash hands and then not use barrier (paper towel) to turn off faucet. Use a barrier to turn off faucet to avoid recontamination of hands. Discussed proper hand washing technique with PIC.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels available for use in men’s restroom. Towels were provided in men’s restroom during inspection.

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed paper towel being used to plug a hole in the walk-in cooler door. Remove paper towel and fill hole with a material that is smooth and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed foods in the walk in cooler to be between 50F and 53F.  The unit was found by the manager to be frozen around 12:30pm. At that time the manager turned the temperature up so that the unit could thaw. Temp log for the morning open stated that the walk in was at 39F.  The manager was going to turn the unit up for a couple of hours and then turn it back down. She said that she turned the unit up at 12:30pm Foods were moved to the walk in freezer and back stock cooler so that the unit could continue to thaw and not hold food out of temperature. The thermometer on the unit read 60F during defrost. 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: Observed no thermometer in the back stock cooler. Two thermometers were found in the make table. The extra thermometer was provided to the back stock unit. An independent thermometer was also added to the walk in cooler. 4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed an employee to put fingers inside of drink cup when handing it to the customer. Employee education will be conducted by manager. 4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Observed multiple rubber parts from some equipment sitting in the hand sink at the start of the inspection. The inspector removed the items from the hand sink. Ensure the hand sink is used for hand washing only. 
(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Observed the area behind the soda nozzles on the drive-thru soda machine to be soiled with mildew and other debris. Ensure this surface is cleaned at a frequency so it is maintained clean.
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: Observed a small leak on the water filter system above the ice machine. The leak is just a drip, but a puddle of water has accumulated behind the ice machine. Ensure this leak is fixed by the next routine inspection. 
A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: Observed the mop sitting inside the mop sink in a position that did not allow it to air dry. 
After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) Ready to eat sandwich ingreedients are observed to be stored below an open bottle of Mt. Dew laying on its side. Store food for the public above empoyee food to protect it from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11. The soda was immediately discarded.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Pepperoni and Salami are 48°F and 47°F  respectively. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B). One reason the food could be out of temperature is that the level of the food was over an inch above the fill line on the pan. Watch and use this guide for safer food storage.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11  (P)  A vaping device is observed to be stored on the prep counter next to the coffee maker. Toxic materials must be stored so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles. Employee moved materials to separated storage. Reference 7-201.11. The vaping device was moved to the proper, provided storage location.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed verde chicken boats to be 49F at 2:10pm. They were set up at 1:20pm. Use time as a control or temperature control in an effective manner.  Manager will cool sauce before adding to chicken and move boats to reach in (back stock cooler) behind the line.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: Observed employee to go from taking money to taking an order at the drive up and then move with the card to begin to make a sandwich with out hand washing. Employee was immediately stopped and coached. Hand washing was conducted. Observed another employee to wash hands and not use a clean barrier to turn off sink after hand washing. Employees were coached.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer in the 3rd part to be less than 200ppm. The dispenser was adjusted with a new nozzle by the manager. The dispenser now delivers 200ppm of quat. 750-820d Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: Observed wet wiping cloth to be hanging on the side of the sanitizing bucket. Keep wiping cloths in proper solution between uses. 750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed a personal drink (soda can) stored intermingled with food for the general public in the walk in cooler. Personal drinks shall have a lid and straw and be stored in a manner that cannot potentially contaminate food (below and away). Food employee removed drink immediately.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee did not wash hands between glove changes. Proper handwashing between tasks and glove changes were discussed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, prior to putting on gloves, between glove changes, and prior to working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - A) Wire shelving above prep table and small wall mounted wire rack were observed with chipped paint. Repaint the shelving and the rack.

B) Plastic bag was observed as a seal for a hole in the walkin cooler door. Provide proper repairs to the walkin cooler door.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) slicer (food debris) - cleaned during inspection; and
B) lobby soda machine - 1. nozzles/diffusers (mold) & 2. ice shoot (mold). 

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The surface of the sprayer at the 3 part sink was observed with general buildup. Clean the surface of the sprayer.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - A) Moisture and debris were observed under the drive thru soda counter. Manager observed the ice bin drain line to be draining onto the floor. The drain line was repositioned to drain properly into the floor drain. Staff began cleaning under the counter during the inspection.

B) Single service articles were observed along the floor to wall juncture behind the handsink. Manager cleaned the area behind the handsink during the inspection.

C) Floor drain under the 3 part sink had a heavy accumulation of buildup in it. Clean the floor drain as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120  - Top layers of chicken strips and teriyaki chicken in cold bain on make line had internal temperatures at 55F and 49F-53F respectivley. Layers of the same product deeper in the pans were 44F/below. Top layers of said products were removed from the cold bain and discarded. (see general comments)

Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage. Make sure cold potentially hazardous foods are stacked below fill lines in pans at the cold baine and kept covered between uses/during slow periods to help maintain products at colder temperatures. **All internal temperatures for foods held in cold bain were at 41F/below**.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - Ceiling inside ice machine had areas where rust is starting to form again. Some mold and lime buildup were also noted. Make repairs inside the ice machine to eliminate rust and allow for ease in cleaning/general maintenance. If proper repairs are not possible it may be time to consider replacing the ice machine.

Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Sanitizer solution was not set up for wiping thermometer between temperature checks. Paper towel was being used to wipe stem of thermometer between products. Manager obtained sanitizer solution (200ppm quat) to use for remainder of temperature checks.

Maintain a separate sanitizer solution for use when doing internal temperature checks. Wipe the stem before and after each product and allow stem to air dry or use a clean paper towel to wipe stem after stem has been wiped with sanitizer cloth.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The soda nozzles and diffuser at lobby soda machine had mold accumulation on them. Nozzles were removed and cleaned/sanitized.

Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.850 - Pans on bottom shelf of prep table used for storage of clean lids, utensils, and equipment were soiled inside with food crumbs/debris. Clean storage pans as needed and maintain them clean. Consider increasing cleaning frequency and also providing a cover of some sort (i.e. lid, etc.) to help minimize buildup of debris in containers.

Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Boxes of single use condiments and sleeves of cups and lids were observed in the cabinet beneath the handsink directly below drain line off the sink. All items were moved to an adjacent cabinet where no plumbing was located. 

Single sue articles shall be stored in a manner that protects items from potential contamination. Do not store single use articles under plumbing - the water going through the drain is form of waste water from handwashing process.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120  - Top layers of steak and chicken strips in cold bain on make line had internal and surface temperatures at 49F-59F. Layers of steak and chicken strips deeper in the pans were 45F/below. Top layers of steak and chicken were removed from the cold bain and placed in the walkin cooler to rapidly drop the temperature. 
Cold potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below at all times during storage. Make sure cold potentially hazardous foods are stacked below fill lines in pans at the cold bain and kept covered between uses/during slow periods to help maintain products at colder temperatures. **All internal temperatures for foods held in cold bain were at 41F/below**.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled with buildup/mold:
A) soda nozzles and diffusers; and
B) ceiling inside ice machine around where ice is made/drops down.
Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.
